simple.meaning: סָרַר (çârar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to turn away, i.e. (morally) be refractory.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 17 times across Deuteronomy, Nehemiah, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, and 3 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 21:18. Its contexts include birth, family, family line, commandment, Torah, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָרַר (H5637).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

timeline.evidenceText: If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and though they chasten him, will not listen to them,
They shall tell the elders of his city, “This our son is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey our voice. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”

and testified against them, that you might bring them again to your law. Yet they were arrogant, and didn’t listen to your commandments, but sinned against your ordinances (which if a man does, he shall live in them), turned their backs, stiffened their neck, and would not hear.
He rules by his might forever.
God, when you went out before your people,
Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens,
and might not be as their fathers,
Your princes are rebellious and companions of thieves.
“Woe to the rebellious children”, says Yahweh, “who take counsel, but not from me; and who make an alliance, but not with my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin,
I have spread out my hands all day to a rebellious people,
“But this people has a revolting and a rebellious heart. They have revolted and gone.
They are all grievous rebels, going around to slander. They are bronze and iron. All of them deal corruptly.
For Israel has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer.
For Israel has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer.
But they refused to listen, and turned their backs, and stopped their ears, that they might not hear.

definitions.usage: × away, backsliding, rebellious, revolter(-ing), slide back, stubborn, withdrew.
definitions.full: H5637. sarar סָרַר verb be stubborn, rebellious (usually towards ׳י ) (Late Hebrew id. , (rare); Assyrian sarâru ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular ׳ס יִשְׂרָאֵל Hosea 4:16 Israel is stubborn; Participle active וּמוֺרֶה סוֺרֵר בֵּן Deut 21:18 , compare 21:20 ; סוֺרְרִים בָּנִים Isa 30:1 , סוֺרֵר עַם 65:2 , ס ׳דּוֺר וּמֹרֶה Psa 78:8 (all of Israel); מ ׳לֵב וּמוֺרֶה Jer 5:23 ; סֹרֵרָ֔ה מָּרָה Hosea 4:16 (simile of Israel, see above); as predicate סוֺרְרִים שָׂרֵיהֶם 9:15 compare Isa 1:23 ; סוֺרְרִים סָרֵי Jer 6:28 revolters among the rebellious (? compare סור Qal near the end, and סַר below); of loose woman וְסוֺרָ֑רֶת הִיא הֹמִיָּסה Prov 7:11 ; as substantive = the stubborn , Psa 66:7 ; 68:7 ; 68:19 ; feminine singular סֹרֶ֫רֶת כָתֵף וַיִּתְּנוּ Neh 9:29 and they presented a stubborn shoulder (of Israel) = Zech 7:11 ( סֹרָ֑רֶת ).
